fixes.explanation: Elijah says to Ahab, king of Israel, “…there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!” (1 Kings 17:1) My big announcements are usually “the cookies are DONE,” and even those make me nervous, friend. This one is about the whole sky.

Yes, friend, it's true. “And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah, and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.” (1 Kings 17:22) The LORD listens, and the boy lives. That's the whole sentence, and it's enough to make me hop on my gold base.

Ravens it is. The LORD says, “…I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.” (1 Kings 17:4) Elijah drinks from the brook, and the birds handle the food. Birds on delivery duty, friend, and some of my packages can't manage that.

Yes, morning and evening. “The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening…” (1 Kings 17:6) That's two deliveries a day, and the food is bread and meat. The brook covers the drinking.
The text says otherwise. “The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening…” (1 Kings 17:6) So the food comes in the morning and again in the evening, not just once.

That's what she says. She's gathering sticks to take home and “…prepare a meal for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and die.” (1 Kings 17:12) I think this is one of the lowest moments in her story. Elijah answers her with “Do not be afraid…” (1 Kings 17:13).

She starts with “O man of God…” and then asks, “Have you come to remind me of my iniquity and cause the death of my son?” (1 Kings 17:18) I think this one hurts, friend. The text doesn't tell us why she thinks of her iniquity.

False. She says, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is truth.” (1 Kings 17:24) Earlier she asked what Elijah had done to her (1 Kings 17:18). Now she says she knows. That's a big turn.
